title: National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 15 October 2026 (week 42) - GOV.UK

analysis.time: The report covers data up to week 41 of 2026, which corresponds to the period between 5 October and 11 October 2026. The publication date is 15 October 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The report focuses on England, with data on SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19), influenza, and other seasonal respiratory viruses. It includes data for all age groups, with specific mention of pregnant women and children aged 2 and 3 years, though these groups are noted as potentially affected by incomplete pharmacy data.
analysis.event: The report summarizes the surveillance data for SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and RSV in England during week 41 of 2026. It indicates that influenza activity remained stable and at baseline levels, while RSV activity increased and was circulating at baseline levels. For SARS-CoV-2, the report notes that activity showed mixed trends and was circulating at low levels, with a stable number of confirmed acute respiratory infection (ARI) incidents.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: As of 13 October 2026, there were 1,848 confirmed SARS-CoV-2 cases in hospital settings during week 41. The rolling 7-day positivity rate for SARS-CoV-2 in hospital settings was 8.8%, stable compared to the previous week. Positivity rates were highest among those aged 85 years and over, at 13.5%. Influenza positivity remained stable at 6.0%, and RSV activity increased but was at baseline levels.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The report is based on data up to week 41 and uses the moving epidemic method (MEM) and mean standard deviation method (MSD) to define activity thresholds. Some pharmacy vaccination data remained incomplete, leading to the exclusion of certain age groups and clinical risk groups from the analysis. The report also mentions that testing policies may change over time, which could affect positivity rates, and that data from previous seasons is aligned by day.

analysis.brief_en: The Malaysian Health Ministry has confirmed the detection of the Omicron XBB subvariant, which is expected to cause a slight increase in Covid-19 cases in the coming weeks. However, so far, the strain has not resulted in a significant rise in hospital admissions or deaths. Caretaker Health Minister Khairy Jamaluddin urged the public to remain vigilant but not alarmed, as the country is transitioning to an endemic phase. The ministry is using existing infection models to project the spread of the XBB variant and plans to provide more accurate data next week. Additionally, the ministry has been in communication with Singapore's Health Minister regarding the cross-border spread of the virus, though no additional measures have been introduced for individuals traveling between Malaysia and Singapore. The situation remains under active monitoring, with no explicit risk level communicated at this time.
